title: Coxeter Diagrams and the Schläfli Order Formula for the Platonic Solids
description: Reconstructs the three Platonic reflection groups A₃, B₃, H₃ from their Coxeter diagrams and reads every invariant straight off the Schläfli symbol {p, q}. Each solid is the linear rank-3 Coxeter path o–p–o–q–o; Platonic duality reverses the diagram (a group isomorphism), which is exactly why the five solids give only three groups. Proves the direct order formula |W| = 8pq/(2p+2q−pq) = 4E, the spherical (finiteness) criterion pq < 2p+2q (with the three Euclidean tilings {3,6},{4,4},{6,3} on the boundary), and the defect denominators 3,2,2,1,1. Fully computational (kernel decide/rfl), 0 axioms. Child of platonic-solids-oq-03.

overview.historicalContext: The identification of a regular polyhedron {p, q} with a Coxeter group predates Coxeter's own diagrams: the symmetry group is generated by reflections in the three planes of a characteristic (fundamental) triangle, whose angles π/p, π/q, π/2 give the Coxeter matrix. Coxeter's linear diagrams o–p–o–q–o (1934) encode exactly this data, and the finiteness (sphericity) of the group is governed by the classical Schläfli inequality 1/p + 1/q > 1/2, whose boundary 1/p + 1/q = 1/2 gives the three Euclidean tilings {3,6}, {4,4}, {6,3}. This entry formalizes the diagram side of the correspondence its parent set up via degrees.
overview.problemStatement: **Correspondence (diagram side).** Every Platonic solid {p, q} is the linear rank-3 Coxeter group with diagram o–p–o–q–o. Reading the invariants off the Schläfli symbol: the group order is |W| = 8pq/(2p+2q−pq) = 4E = d₁d₂d₃; the solid is spherical exactly when pq < 2p+2q; and Platonic duality (p ↔ q) reverses the diagram — a group isomorphism, so duals share their group and the five solids give only three.
overview.text: Formalizes the Coxeter-diagram datum of each solid, the reversal isomorphism explaining the three symmetry classes, the direct Schläfli order formula, and the spherical finiteness criterion — all as finite decidable identities in the parent's style.
overview.proofStrategy:
All statements reduce to finite numerical/structural identities verified by the kernel `decide`, `rfl`, or case analysis on the five-element `Solid` (deliberately avoiding `native_decide`).

1. A `CoxDiagram` records the two bond labels (a, b) = (m₁₂, m₂₃) of a linear rank-3 diagram (the outer bond m₁₃ = 2 is implicit); `diagram s = ⟨p, q⟩` reads them off the Schläfli symbol.
2. Reversal `⟨a,b⟩ ↦ ⟨b,a⟩` models reading the path from the other end; `dual_reverses_diagram` is `cases s <;> rfl`, and `normalize_reverse` uses `min`/`max` commutativity so the sorted diagram is reversal-invariant.
3. `normalize_determines_coxeter` is a 5×5 case split proving equal normalised diagrams force equal reflection groups; composing with `dual_normalize_diagram` recovers `coxeter (dual s) = coxeter s` purely from the diagram.
4. The defect `2p+2q−pq` and the order `8pq/defect` are evaluated per solid; `decide` checks `8pq/defect = |W| = 4E` (exact ℕ-division for all five).
5. Sphericity `pq < 2p+2q` is decidable; the five solids satisfy it, the boundary tilings {3,6},{4,4},{6,3} do not, and sphericity ⇔ positive defect.
keyInsights: The Coxeter diagram is the second canonical datum (alongside the degrees) pinning a reflection group down: for {p,q} it is the path o–p–o–q–o, so the whole group is encoded by the pair (p, q).

Platonic duality is diagram reversal: {p,q} ↦ {q,p} reflects the linear diagram about its centre. Since a Coxeter group is unchanged by reversing its diagram, duals share a group — the structural reason five solids give three groups (cube {4,3} and octahedron {3,4} are mirror diagrams of the same B₃).
The order is computable straight from the Schläfli symbol: |W| = 8pq/(2p+2q−pq), reproducing 4E and the product-of-degrees without any group theory.

Finiteness is the Schläfli inequality 1/p + 1/q > 1/2 ⇔ pq < 2p+2q; the Platonic solids are its strict interior and the three Euclidean tilings {3,6},{4,4},{6,3} sit exactly on the boundary (defect 0), where the order formula's denominator vanishes.

sections.title: Module Overview and Honest Scope
sections.summary: Docstring: the Coxeter-diagram side of the Platonic ↔ Coxeter correspondence — diagram o–p–o–q–o, duality as reversal, the Schläfli order formula, and the spherical criterion, all at the numerical-invariant level.
sections.mathContext: A finite reflection group of {p,q} is the linear rank-3 Coxeter group with bonds (p,q); constructing the concrete groups and proving |W|=∏dᵢ intrinsically is out of scope (absent from Mathlib).

sections.title: The Coxeter Diagram of a Schläfli Symbol
sections.summary: `CoxDiagram` (bond labels a=m₁₂, b=m₂₃; outer bond m₁₃=2 implicit), `diagram s = ⟨p,q⟩`, the diagram of each solid, and the canonical A₃=[3,3], B₃=[4,3], H₃=[5,3].
sections.mathContext: The Coxeter matrix of {p,q} has m₁₂=p, m₂₃=q, m₁₃=2 — a path (linear) diagram. The bond pair (p,q) is the second canonical datum for the group alongside the degrees.

sections.title: Duality Reverses the Diagram (and Preserves the Group)
sections.summary: Diagram reversal ⟨a,b⟩↦⟨b,a⟩ (involution); duality reverses the diagram; the normalised (sorted-bond) diagram is reversal-invariant and determines the reflection group, recovering coxeter(dual s)=coxeter(s) from the diagram.
sections.mathContext: Reversing a Coxeter diagram yields an isomorphic group; Platonic duality is exactly this reversal, so the five solids realize only three groups (their diagrams fall into three reversal classes).

sections.title: The Direct Schläfli Order Formula
sections.summary: The defect denominator 2p+2q−pq (values 3,2,2,1,1) and the order formula |W| = 8pq/(2p+2q−pq), shown equal to the parent's |W| and to 4E for every solid.
sections.mathContext: The classical order of the spherical group [p,q] is 8pq/(2p+2q−pq); exact ℕ-division holds precisely because each solid is spherical (positive defect).

sections.title: The Spherical (Finiteness) Criterion
sections.summary: `isSpherical p q := pq < 2p+2q` (decidable); all five solids are spherical; the boundary tilings {3,6},{4,4},{6,3} are not; sphericity ⇔ positive defect.
sections.mathContext: 1/p+1/q>1/2 (spherical/finite), =1/2 (Euclidean/infinite tilings), <1/2 (hyperbolic). The Platonic solids are the strict interior; the three regular tilings sit on the boundary.

sections.title: Capstone Correspondence
sections.summary: `schlafli_coxeter_correspondence`: for every solid the diagram is ⟨p,q⟩, |W| = 8pq/(2p+2q−pq) = 4E, the solid is spherical, and duality reverses the diagram while preserving the group.
sections.mathContext: Bundles the diagram, order-formula, sphericity and duality facts into a single per-solid statement, mirroring the parent's invariant-level capstone from the diagram side.

conclusion.summary: This child reconstructs the three Platonic reflection groups from their Coxeter diagrams rather than their degrees, and reads every invariant off the Schläfli symbol {p, q}: the diagram is the path o–p–o–q–o, the order is 8pq/(2p+2q−pq) = 4E = d₁d₂d₃, and the solid is spherical exactly when pq < 2p+2q. Platonic duality is shown to be diagram reversal — a group isomorphism — giving the structural reason the five solids realize only three groups.
conclusion.implications:
1. **Diagram side of the correspondence**: complements the parent's degree-based invariants with the Coxeter-diagram datum and the direct Schläfli order formula.

2. **Duality made structural**: duals share a group because reversing a Coxeter diagram is an isomorphism, not merely because their tabulated orders agree.

3. **Finiteness criterion**: exhibits the Schläfli inequality 1/p+1/q>1/2 and its Euclidean boundary concretely, isolating the Platonic list as the strict spherical interior.
openQuestions: Can the Coxeter matrix (with the m₁₃=2 outer bond) be promoted to an actual presented group ⟨s₁,s₂,s₃ | (sᵢsⱼ)^{mᵢⱼ}⟩ in Lean and its order proved intrinsically?
Can diagram reversal be upgraded from an equality of invariants to an explicit group isomorphism of the constructed groups?
Does the full rank-3 spherical classification (A₃, B₃, H₃ and the dihedral I₂(m)) follow from enumerating linear diagrams under the Schläfli inequality?
